questions.question: Arrange the six levels of ecological study from smallest to largest, define population and ecosystem exactly, and state the key difference between a community and an ecosystem.
questions.expected_answer: Organism, population, community, ecosystem, biome, biosphere. Population: all the individuals of one species living in the same area at the same time. Ecosystem: a community of living organisms together with its non-living environment, with all the interactions between them. A community includes only living things (all the populations of an area); an ecosystem adds the abiotic environment.

questions.question: For a farm dam, list four biotic and four abiotic components, and explain which column a dead fish floating on the surface belongs in and why.
questions.expected_answer: Biotic: fish, reeds, frogs, algae, water birds, bacteria, dead organic matter. Abiotic: water, sunlight, temperature, mud/soil, rocks, dissolved oxygen, wind. The dead fish is biotic: it is material from a living organism and is still being used by decomposers; only things that were never alive are abiotic.

questions.question: Define habitat and give two South African examples. Then describe one seasonal change and an organism's adaptation to it, stating how the adaptation helps survival.
questions.expected_answer: A habitat is the kind of place where an organism lives, which provides its food, water, shelter and space (described by physical features). Examples: rocky koppie for a dassie; muddy dam bottom for a barbel; riverine bush for a leopard. Seasonal change e.g. the dry Lowveld winter: marula/baobab trees drop their leaves to reduce water loss when roots cannot take up enough water; or the African bullfrog aestivates buried in mud in a skin cocoon until rain returns, avoiding drying out; or swallows migrate to Europe when food becomes scarce.
